svg.title: Pylon system map: wallets, terminal, Rust service, Mezo Testnet
svg.desc: Architecture of Pylon: user wallets and an x402 agent on the left, a Next.js terminal and a Rust service (indexer, solver, keeper, x402 gateway) in the middle, and the live Mezo Testnet contracts on the right — Mezo core, the Tigris pools, and the three Pylon contracts — separated by a marked trust boundary.
svg.text: A terminal and a Rust service off-chain · Mezo core, Tigris and three Pylon contracts on-chain

g.text: What is already live on Mezo (core contracts, Tigris pools), what Pylon
added (three contracts), and where the trust boundaries actually sit —
the part a judge should attack first.
one EIP-712 signature lets the engine act on your trove
system + trove interest · the exact debt lives here
the redemption queue · insert hints in one call
an ERC-20 transfer moves native BTC
the flash venue · ~201k MUSD · 0.01% fee · hook()
a pool cannot be swapped inside its own callback
swap() + hook() · EIP-712 exact amounts · fee split
owns its own trove · permissionless defend()

svg.text: TRUST BOUNDARIES · WHAT PYLON CANNOT DO — 1 · 2 · 3 MARK THE DASHED LINE

g.text: the service builds and submits, but it can
never sign for you: every amount moved is
shield loans only go to positions the engine
registered: capped per call, per position,
and by an on-chain utilisation ceiling.
a position with a shield loan outstanding
cannot withdraw collateral — the claim is
enforced in the contract, not by us.
